name: Anubis
description: Anubis is a reverse proxy that sits in front of a web service and stops AI scrapers and abusive bots with a proof-of-work challenge, while letting real browsers and well-behaved crawlers through.

app_vars.name: var_anubis_target
app_vars.label: Upstream URL to protect
app_vars.help: The service Anubis proxies to, e.g. http://192.168.1.50:3000. Can be changed later in /etc/anubis/main.env

notes.text: Set TARGET in /etc/anubis/main.env to the service you want to protect, then run `systemctl restart anubis@main`. Point your reverse proxy or DNS at this container on port 8923.

The container is configured for direct exposure over plain HTTP (COOKIE_SECURE=false, USE_REMOTE_ADDRESS=true). When you put a TLS reverse proxy in front of it, set COOKIE_SECURE=true and remove USE_REMOTE_ADDRESS so client IPs come from X-Forwarded-For.

One Anubis instance protects one TARGET. For another service, copy /etc/anubis/main.env to /etc/anubis/<name>.env with its own BIND, METRICS_BIND and TARGET and run `systemctl enable --now anubis@<name>`. Alternatively point TARGET at a reverse proxy that routes by Host header and a single instance covers all its sites.
Bot policies live in /etc/anubis/main.botPolicies.yaml (a copy of the upstream default). Prometheus metrics are exposed on port 9090.
